title.narrative: International Trade Center - SME inom ukrainskt jordbruk, fas 2 2021-2025
International Trade Center Agribusiness SMEs Phase 2 2021-2025

description.narrative:
Impact. The Phase II will contribute to enhanced competitiveness and sustained export growth of the Ukrainian SMEs in the fruits, vegetables, nuts and wine sectors.
Phase II will also contribute to job creation; economic empowerment of women; and minimization of the environmental footprint by introducing principles of sustainable production practices and standards. The expected outcome of Phase II is enhanced competitiveness and internationalization of SMEs from the selected sectors as well as the enablement of BSOs to provide relevant services to enterprises.
Phase II is also structured around four outputs:
Output 1. Roadmap updated and/or developed for selected value chains. It is planned to update roadmaps for fruits and vegetables. The roadmap for nuts is currently being developed by the project. The roadmap for the wine sector will be designed using the value chain approach and priorities set in cooperation with relevant stakeholders and producers. The expected results of Output 1 will be the number roadmaps/strategies developed/updated and endorsed by stakeholders, as well as the increased capacity of relevant stakeholders and local authorities to understand and set strategic priorities for the development of the sectors concerned.
Output 2. Capacities of SMEs strengthened to improve their international competitiveness. The project will assist selected SMEs from the selected sectors to reinforce and enlarge their presence in the market and increase exports. The project will enhance SME capacities through awareness building, training, advisory services, and study tours. The scope will include building competencies in growing, harvesting, post-harvesting, packaging, logistics, marketing and sales, branding, CSR, as well as in business planning and management.
Output 3. Capacities of sectoral BSOs strengthened to provide SMEs with relevant business support services. The project will also continue to enhance BSOs capacities, enlarge their service offerings to SMEs and develop operational and managerial performance. The scope of BSOs capacity building will cover supply chain management, quality assurance and certification, trade intelligence, market analysis, and research, sales, export strategy. To ensure sustainability, the project will anchor knowledge sharing platforms within partner BSOs, help them to integrate into international networks, and establish mechanisms for cooperation.
Output 4. Market linkages created for SMEs from fruits, vegetables and nuts sectors to expand their sales domestically and internationally (in particular, with a focus on the EU market). The major focus of the project will be to assist companies to establish market linkages leading to tangible results.

International Trade Center (ITC) har ansökt till Sida om ett bidrag på 20 003 805 SEK för att genomföra insatsen "ITC - SME inom ukrainskt jordbruk, fas 2" i Ukraina under perioden 2021-2024. Insatsen är en fortsättning av "ITC – SME och värdekedjor inom ukrainskt jordbruk " (PLANit 55070084) som avslutas i april 2021.
Målet med insatsen är att stödja ukrainska små och medelstora företag inom frukt- och grönsaksodlingssektorn att integreras i inhemska och globala värdekedjor och få tillgång till nya marknader genom att: - stödja små och medelstora företag att producera varor i enlighet med marknadens krav - stärka kapaciteten hos företagsstödorganisationer (BSO) att tillhandahålla kvalitativa tjänster för att utveckla små och medelstora företag, och - länka små och medelstora företag till utvalda marknader med fokus på EU.
Interventionen kommer att genomföras av ett projektkontor som ITC har etablerat i Ukraina, med stöd av huvudkontoret i Genève.
Insatsens totala budget är 20 003 805 kr. Sida är den enda finansiären. Ingen vidarebefordran av medel är planerad inom insatsen.

International Trade Center (ITC) has applied to Sida for funding of SEK 20 003 805 to carry out the "ITC Ukrainian agribusiness SMEs phase 2" in Ukraine during the period 2021-2024. This contribution is a continuation of the contribution 'ITC Ukrainian agribusiness SMEs and value chains' (PLANit 55070084) that is coming to an end in April 2021.
The goal of the contribution is to support Ukrainian SMEs in the fruits and vegetables sector integrating into domestic and global value chains and accessing new markets by: - assisting SMEs to produce goods in accordance with market requirements - improving the capacities of Business Support Organizations (BSOs) to provide quality business support services to SMEs, and - linking SMEs to target markets, with a focus on the EU.
The intervention will be implemented by an ITC project office established in Ukraine with the support of Geneva HQ.
The intervention’s total budget is SEK 20 003 805. There is no other than Sida funding. There is no forwarding of funds in this contribution.

description.narrative:
Reporting during the year has been a bit meager. In April, a project meeting at the Embassy in Kyiv was held between the project team (represented by National Project Manager based in Odessa and Programme Coordinator, based in Geneva) and programme officers from the Embassy as well as Stockholm. During 2024, export is continuing, e g to the Middle East and to Malaysia by boat, but only in the premium segment with products at higher prices. Some new markets have been established and the trade fairs are absolutely crucial to continue to attend. Some key take-aways from the meeting: - Trade fairs are of highest priority and should not be dropped - At this point, survival for the business is the only focus - When there will be stability again, the focus of the project will be to restructure and to develop the SMEs
A mid term review, that also served as the final evaluation, was carried out during the spring and delivered to Sida in April. Some findings included that the project was relevant at the time of its design and became even more relevant since the war with Russia started, but the budget was small for the enlarged scope. The project did not have explicit component on policy advice, but through the Sectoral Roadmaps it affected the improvements in the regulatory environment, especially in the vine and wine sector. It was efficient, cost effective and the management displayed strong adaptive qualities in the face of adversities, that included the war and the COVID.
However, the evaluation stated that the project would not likely to reach some of its targets, mainly due to the war. However, it trained more companies and people than planned, helped them improve their capacities, and supported more participation in trade fairs than planned. Many companies are likely to report higher employment at the project close. It helped to enhance the capacities of the BSOs, but the progress was slow, due to the war, among other reasons. Some businesses expressed a desire for the project to resume B2B support and support trade missions.
Since the project approached the end of the agreement at the same time as the evaluation was carried out, the discussions on how to proceed was taken place simultaneously. In general, Sida have been content with the previous two phases of project (Phase I 2015-2021, phase II 2021-2024) and have seen some positive results over this period. However, Sida has decided not to continue with a third phase based on the following:
- The project started almost 10 years ago, it is Sida's practise not to have longer projects - The project was relevant when it was designed, but the context has changed - Sida is building a new portfolio with focus on reconstruction and with new priorities, Sida has a strong focus on the energy sector - The project has had difficulties in strengthening the capacities of Business Service Organisations that should be providing support to SMEs, which Sida would have liked to see more of.
The project requested a no-cost extension of the activity period until April 2025 to finalise the project activities, and Sida has approved the extension.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
